notes:
Inbound SMB lead via self-serve signup (trial credit used). Wants hosted API for customer support chat + light tool-calling for order lookup. Primary pain: streaming JSON mode and function-calling schemas are brittle in their tests.

Initial contact: AE outreach 2026-02-19 — interested but cautious on cost + reliability. Did a quick demo of hosted streaming and function-calls on 2026-02-25 (see Fireflies ff-20260225-01-bonsai-demo).

Customer-reported symptoms (from SE pairing run 2026-03-03):
- When enabling streaming with JSON-mode output, clients intermittently receive partial JSON fragments (model emits trailing commas or unclosed arrays) causing downstream parser failures.
- Function schema mismatch: their front-end generates a function signature (camelCase) while model examples in Redwood SDK use snake_case; when model attempts to call functions, Redwood Hosted proxies return 400 with "schema mismatch" during reroute.
- Observed increased latency when using streaming + tool-calls together; suspect excessive round trips to tool proxy.

Environment/usage profile:
- Small fleet of web support agents (40 seats). Peak concurrency ~30 sessions. Typical prompt length short (context windows ~512 tokens), average response length ~150 tokens. Cost-sensitive but values reliability; wants predictable failover behaviour.
- Using public cloud region us-west-2. No Private/VPC requirement for now.

What we've tried (notes from SE):
- Reproduced partial JSON in staging using same prompt templates. Root cause appears to be model continuation strategy combined with streaming chunk boundaries; model sometimes emits filler/newline before finishing object.
- Temporary workaround: post-stream reassembly + tolerant parser with trailing-comma handling and final-JSON-validation step. Customer dislikes workaround (adds complexity).
- Adjusted generation settings: set stop tokens, increased temperature -> reduced occurrences but not eliminated.
- Mapped frontend function names to server-side canonical schema via a lightweight adapter; this resolved immediate 400s but not ideal long term.

Open questions / asks from customer:
